review_output: {"summary":"Not a sign-off. A BLOCKER remains: the Serializable order-update gate still fails (6/20, versus 16/20 with only the metric trigger disabled). The trigger contributes to the failures but is not the only cause, and the full root cause is still unknown. Verified by code reading: read-time count rechecks fail closed for stale ready reports; append-only events plus the delete and truncate blocks keep the count monotonic; existing reports are marked stale. Assumptions not yet checked: the worker and reader DB role (revokes and RLS could make COUNT fail or silently return 0), sourceRevision coverage of non-order joins, and deployed retry/timer recovery. Still required: find and fix the Serializable root cause and pass the gate, verify runtime roles, bound the cost of COUNT, and run an HTTP/provider/timer recovery test against a deployed environment.","findings":[{"area":"Payment concurrency","severity":"BLOCKER","confidence":0.9,"file":"20261015140000_live_metric_order_source/migration.sql","issue":"Serializable order-update gate still FAILS; trigger measurably worsens it but the root cause is unknown.","evidence":"Supplied evidence: 6/20 with trigger, 16/20 with only this trigger disabled, still failing. On the paths that pass the early-return check, the trigger reads PaymentTransaction and Live and runs an FK KEY SHARE check on Vendor. Observed: order PK tuple and page predicate locks.","impact":"Payment writes depend on retries; the WP cannot pass its gate. Don't call the trigger the sole cause.","recommended_fix":"Capture pg_locks/SIREAD and the conflict-out pairs per failure. Check whether trigger lookups fall back to seq scans (a relation-level SIREAD). Consider deferring source capture out of the Serializable tx, e.g. an outbox written with no reads.","required_test":"20+ synchronized Serializable updates hit the success threshold with trigger enabled; conflicts are categorized by lock type."},{"area":"Privileges/RLS","severity":"MAJOR","confidence":0.6,"file":"both migrations; live-metric-report-reader.ts","issue":"Create/claim/finish/guard/readers are SECURITY INVOKER and COUNT LiveMetricOrderSource, which has RLS enabled, no policies, and API-role revokes.","evidence":"REVOKE ALL from service_role/authenticated. No policy exists. The worker role config is unverified.","impact":"Assumption, not verified: an API role gets permission denied. A role granted SELECT without BYPASSRLS silently counts 0, so the revision stops invalidating.","recommended_fix":"Expose the count through a narrow SECURITY DEFINER function, or add an explicit worker policy. Document the runtime roles.","required_test":"Using the actual worker and app roles, COUNT equals the owner COUNT after events, and a stale report becomes unavailable."},{"area":"Count scalability","severity":"MAJOR","confidence":0.75,"file":"live-metric-report-reader.ts","issue":"COUNT(*) per scope runs on every page read and every ready-report read. The immutable table grows without bound (old and new scope rows per change).","evidence":"reportSnapshot and readMetricIntervalPage recount per page (up to 4000 pages). Inside one RR snapshot the count is constant, so this is redundant.","impact":"O(pages×events) work, dashboard read amplification, and a 30s budget that hot lives could exhaust.","recommended_fix":"Count once per RR transaction and reuse it. Benchmark index-only scans and vacuum. Design a compaction/checkpoint that is safe under the scope lock.","required_test":"Benchmark with 1e5–1e6 events per scope, measuring worker and ready-read latency."},{"area":"Source invalidation","severity":"MAJOR","confidence":0.5,"file":"live-metric-report-reader.ts","issue":"The order reader also depends on FormSubmission, RegistrationForm, Live.formId/vendorId and LiveMetricRegistration, which this trigger doesn't cover.","evidence":"The trigger watches only order/payment columns. Coverage of these through sourceRevision is assumed, not verified.","impact":"Changes to those tables could leave stale ready results.","recommended_fix":"Prove that every joined column bumps sourceRevision, or emit events for it.","required_test":"Mutate each joined column after ready, then readMetricReadyReport returns unavailable."},{"area":"Recovery","severity":"MAJOR","confidence":0.7,"file":"payment webhook path (supplied evidence)","issue":"18/20 first-attempt 500s are recovered only by a manual sequential retryWebhookEvent.","evidence":"Direct Request invocation; no deployed HTTP, provider, or timer. The source failure test still FAILS.","impact":"Production recovery depends on an unverified scheduler and provider retry behavior.","recommended_fix":"Verify the timer/worker under concurrency and with the real provider retry schedule.","required_test":"Deployed end-to-end run: 20 concurrent callbacks recover automatically within maxRetries."},{"area":"Lifecycle","severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.7,"file":"20261015150000_live_metric_order_report_binding/migration.sql","issue":"Claim/finish compute the count before taking the version lock. If events arrive in between, the guard raises an exception instead of returning 0 and marking the report stale.","evidence":"order_revision is read before FOR UPDATE; the guard recounts in a fresh RC statement.","impact":"Fails closed, but the worker sees errors and the report stays queued until a later claim.","recommended_fix":"Count after the lock, or catch the error and mark the report stale.","required_test":"Inject an event between the count and the lock; claim returns 0 and the report is stale."},{"area":"Privileges","severity":"MINOR","confidence":0.55,"file":"20261015140000_live_metric_order_source/migration.sql","issue":"The sequence is revoked only from PUBLIC. Supabase default privileges may still grant sequence access to the API roles.","evidence":"The DO loop omits LiveMetricOrderSource_id_seq.","impact":"API roles could burn IDs; low risk.","recommended_fix":"Revoke the sequence from the API roles in the loop.","required_test":"has_sequence_privilege returns false for each API role."},{"area":"Immutability","severity":"NIT","confidence":0.6,"file":"20261015140000_live_metric_order_source/migration.sql","issue":"ON UPDATE CASCADE on vendorId is blocked by the immutable trigger, so a Vendor id update fails once any event exists.","evidence":"The trigger allows only DELETE when the vendor is gone.","impact":"Probably intended; confirm.","recommended_fix":"Use ON UPDATE RESTRICT, or document the behavior.","required_test":"A Vendor id update behaves as specified."}]}
